topics.label: Introduction to the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture's learning outcomes and provides an overview of the hallmarks of cancer and tumor progression models.

topics.label: Growth signaling pathways and proliferative independence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how oncogenic alterations in key signaling cascades, including Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinase pathways, enable self-sufficient growth in cancer cells.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired terminal differentiation prevents cells from exiting the cell cycle and promotes tumor development in both hematological and epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence bypass, and p53 stress surveillance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening and cellular stress induce senescence via p53 pathways, and how cancer cells bypass these tumor-suppressive barriers through telomerase reactivation.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce complex cancer hallmarks and examine the mechanisms of tumor metabolic rewiring, including aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations producing oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction and regulation of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumors stimulate new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and ensure nutrient supply.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the biological steps, clinical detection, environmental determinants, and genomic features associated with cancer metastasis.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic summarizes the overall integration of cancer hallmarks and concludes the lecture.
